source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Digoxin should always be taken fasting because any food intake prevents clinically meaningful absorption of the medication.","B":"Digoxin may be taken with or without food, but consistent timing is useful and very high-fiber meals can reduce its absorption.","C":"High-fiber food increases digoxin absorption, so the dose should routinely be reduced whenever the medication is taken with breakfast.","D":"Meal timing and dietary fiber have no effect on digoxin absorption, so consistency relative to meals provides no practical benefit."}}
source_row.rationale: While digoxin can generally be taken with or without food, taking it consistently (around the same time relative to meals each day) helps support more predictable absorption and drug levels. High-fiber foods taken at the same time as digoxin may somewhat reduce its absorption, so general consistency in timing is a helpful teaching point.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed digoxin labeling, Clinical Pharmacology 12.3 Absorption: meals slow absorption rate; high-bran fiber can reduce amount absorbed. Current DailyMed label reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
